title: State-contingent sovereign debt: payment dominance, exact comparability and implementable bounds
oneLine: A duration veto can reject a debt contract that pays less at every date; exact certificates expose the conflict and give sharp payment bounds under declared information.
abstract: This candidate studies exact verification and design under a declared three-coordinate sovereign-debt comparability screen. Present value and programme service are affine on each trigger region, while duration gives a quadratic inequality. An explicit construction pays less at every date and passes both endpoint tests yet fails duration throughout the interior; a perturbation makes both endpoints pass strictly. A payment-removal identity characterises when duration respects componentwise reductions. Exact interval methods then give implementable payment bounds under partial information. In a new nonproportional family with unmatched old claims and an oblique trigger, the sharp cap is 25 off-trigger and 110/7 on-trigger, with the binding constraint switching at uplift 75/7. A separate checker reconstructs every certified domain and trigger region from the declared model before checking 48 minima and 252 coefficient identities. These are conditional mathematical results, not an authenticated contract analysis, welfare result, sustainability assessment or country verdict.
keyResults: A candidate cash flow can be componentwise smaller than the reference, pass both endpoint duration tests strictly, and still fail a separate duration veto at interior states.
For the declared piecewise-affine model, exact verification reduces on each reachable trigger region to two affine inequalities and one quadratic inequality, with finite facewise certificates.
A nonproportional oblique-trigger family has sharp payment caps 25 and 110/7 in its two regions; duration becomes binding exactly when the uplift exceeds 75/7.
evidence: Self-contained written proofs and exact rational code. The producer and an implementation-diverse checker reconstruct the declared inputs separately. The checker rebuilds 16 model domains and 10 trigger regions from source data, verifies 48 exact minima, 252 coefficient-determining identities and two sharp scalar intervals, and rejects a self-consistent shortened-domain mutation. Normal and optimised Python runs pass. These are producer-coordinated checks, not unaffiliated reproduction, proof-assistant verification or external peer review.

narration:
Less paid. Still rejected. An Evidence Press briefing.

Suppose a restructured debt contract pays less than a reference contract at every date. It may seem obvious that the lighter contract must pass any reasonable burden-sharing test. This mathematical candidate shows why one particular duration veto can disagree.

Duration is a weighted average payment time. Removing a late payment can lower the total amount owed while also bringing that average time forward. In an exact example, both endpoint states pass the duration test, but every interior state fails. A small perturbation makes both endpoint tests pass strictly, so equality at the boundary is not the explanation.

The paper derives an exact identity showing when removing a payment raises or lowers duration. It then separates three checks: present value, service during a programme window, and duration. On each declared trigger region, the first two are affine and the third becomes a quadratic inequality. This permits exact certificates rather than a numerical grid.

The strongest extension uses two state variables and an oblique trigger. One early payment must be chosen before the later state is known. Off trigger, programme service allows at most twenty-five. On trigger, duration lowers the sharp cap to one hundred and ten sevenths. As the late uplift changes, the binding constraint switches exactly at seventy-five sevenths.

These numbers belong to constructed cash flows and a stipulated rule. Institutional comparability may permit substitutions and consider features that this separate three-veto screen omits. The paper does not authenticate a contract, recommend a restructuring, rank welfare, assess sustainability, or issue a country verdict.

The public package includes the self-contained paper, exact inputs, certificates, an implementation-diverse checker, negative controls and accessible formats. This remains an anonymous, AI-assisted, unrefereed candidate. This briefing uses an AI-generated voice and is not additional scientific evidence.
